name: Garlic / ginseng / aloe scalp remedies

lead: Garlic, ginseng and aloe vera are among the plant ingredients people apply to the scalp as home remedies for hair loss.
The sources reviewed contain no hair-growth studies of them.

paras: Users apply juices, gels or extracts to the scalp, usually describing a stimulating or soothing effect. No mechanism for hair growth was established in the sources reviewed.
Wikipedia reports burns from topical garlic and possible rash or allergy from aloe gel. Ginseng has listed side effects when taken orally.

lead: Garlic, ginseng and aloe vera are plant-based ingredients that circulate as folk or natural topical remedies for hair loss and scalp health, applied as raw preparations, juices, gels or in commercial products.
The Wikipedia articles on each plant do not describe hair-growth research [1][2][3]. They do document safety points relevant to topical use, notably burns reported from topical garlic [1].

paras: Garlic has been applied to the skin in naturopathic practice and for acne. Wikipedia reports serious burns from such use, including in children, and discourages topical use of raw garlic [1].

Panax ginseng is a root used in East Asian folk medicine. Wikipedia states there is little evidence of health effects and lists common side effects such as headache, raised blood pressure, insomnia and rash [2].

Aloe gel is used for minor burns and skin conditions, and cosmetic companies add aloe derivatives to shampoos, with a review attributing this to a moisturizing emollient effect. Wikipedia describes the evidence for wound and burn use as conflicting and notes possible burning, rash or allergic reactions [3].
No studies found for these ingredients as scalp or hair-loss remedies in the sources reviewed.
